question: Which CRM features matter most for running a small residential roofing company ($1.8M/yr, 15-19 jobs/mo, storm/insurance + retail replacement work, solo owner + crews, one office) — and which are worth adding to a lean custom CRM that already has a pipeline board, calendar, weekly attribution reports, and estimate logging?
subQuestions: Which features do the leading roofing CRMs (AccuLynx, JobNimbus, Roofr, Leap, RoofSnap, ServiceTitan, Contractor Foreman) treat as core for residential roofers — and which get adopted vs sit as shelf-ware?

What do roofers themselves (Reddit, roofing forums, Facebook groups, verified reviews on G2/Capterra/SoftwareAdvice) say they use daily, and what do they complain the big CRMs get wrong (bloat, price, complexity, lock-in)?
What storm/insurance-specific workflow features matter: claim tracking fields, adjuster meeting coordination, supplements tracking, Xactimate artifacts, contingency agreements?
What post-sale production/operations features matter: production scheduling boards, crew assignment, material ordering, photo documentation, punch lists, warranty registration?
What sales/follow-up features drive revenue at this size: aging/no-contact alerts, follow-up sequences, commission tracking, per-job costing/profit?
checklist: roofer forum/review voice (what's actually used daily)
common complaints / what NOT to build
stopCondition: Every checklist topic touched by at least one credible source, with the roofer-voice lens (forums/reviews) genuinely exercised — vendor marketing alone does not count as coverage.
